title: fix(browser.action): playbooks use export const action, --play takes relative paths, chromium install gets a skill
description:
## .what

three gaps in `browser.action` / `browser.start`, met while a playbook ran from another repo (dev-env-setup, 2026-11-22).

## .the export contract — keep `export const action`

the loader demands `export const action = async ({ page, browser }) => {...}`; `howto.browser-action-playbooks` documents `export default async (page, ctx)`. a reader who follows the brief gets `playbook must export an action function`.

- **prefer the `export const action` pattern**: a named export, greppable, and the loader already enforces it
- fix the brief (and every example in the role) to match the loader; add no `export default` fallback
- the refusal should print the expected shape: `export const action = async ({ page }) => { ... }`

## .`--play` takes a relative path

`--play .temp/x.play.ts` is read as a package name; `--play ./.temp/x.play.ts` is looked up against the skill dir inside node_modules. only an absolute path works.

- anchor a non-absolute `--play` at the caller cwd before import (join it onto `process.cwd()`)

## .chromium install has no skill

`browser.start` refuses with "chromium not found" and hints a raw `npx playwright install chromium`, which a permission hook blocks.

- ship a skill (e.g. `browser.chromium.set`) that runs the role-pinned playwright cli `install chromium`; idempotent, no sudo
- name that skill in the `browser.start` refusal
- the box-wide libs stay a host concern (sudo + playwright install-deps)

## .acceptance

- a playbook with `export const action` runs via a repo-relative `--play`
- every brief example matches the loader contract
- a box with no chromium gets a refusal that names a runnable skill
